newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade students protest to lift police barriers.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade students protest to lift police barriers.

text.p: Student protesters in Belgrade lined up in front of a police cordon on Thursday at the start of a blockade to test the will of police preventing their daily anti-government marches.
Groups of demonstrators will rotate every hour and student leaders say their "24 hours on the street -- them or us" protest will continue until the police let them pass.
"Our shift is until the morning," said one policeman in the cordon. "Everything depends on the students and their behaviour. If they do not provoke us, throw stones or anything, nothing will happen."
The demonstrators carried handbills urging the police to join their movement.
Thursday marked the 53rd day of protests against the cancellation of local election results by President Slobodan Milosevic's ruling Socialists last November.
On Wednesday, Milosevic conceded that the opposition Zajedno coalition had won in Nis, Serbia's second city, but Zajedno leaders vowed protests would continue until all their claims were met.
